chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father (peace be upon him) disliked being treated/healed with bitter water and with sulphuric water, and he used to say: 'Indeed, Noah (peace be upon him), when the flood occurred, called upon the waters, so all of them responded to him except for the bitter water and the sulphuric water, so he supplicated against them and cursed them both.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams dislike using bitter and sulphuric water for healing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), disliked using bitter water and sulphuric water for medical treatment. He explained this by citing the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him), who called upon all waters during the flood, but they did not respond except for bitter and sulphuric water, leading him to curse them. This tradition highlights the Shia scholarly view of 'causal aversion' (karahat tanzih or tahrimi), where specific natural elements are imbued with spiritual significance based on prophetic precedent, influencing both physical health practices and metaphysical understanding of creation.
